one_line: Regulators tighten AI data rules, massive capex drives market swings, infrastructure expands, and safety safeguards intensify.

themes.title: Regulators shape AI data rules
themes.text: The UK High Court upheld Ofcom’s data‑request notices, while OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic introduced a joint robots.txt opt‑out token, and India’s MeitY published a DEPA handbook for secure AI data sharing.

stories.headline: UK high court rejects Meta, TikTok and X challenge to Ofcom data requests
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic adopt shared robots.txt opt‑out standard
MeitY releases DEPA handbook to enable trusted data sharing for AI training

themes.title: AI capex fuels market turbulence
themes.text: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle disclosed over $3 trillion in data‑center commitments, and investors reacted with steep declines in US tech stocks as AI spending nears $1 trillion, including a 28% fall in Intel shares after a weak outlook.

stories.headline: Big tech firms commit over $3 trillion to AI data‑center spending
US tech stocks tumble as AI spending approaches $1 trillion
Big tech AI capex sparks cash‑flow concerns, stocks tumble
Intel stock falls 28% after weak Q4 outlook, erasing $12B from US government stake

themes.title: AI infrastructure projects scale up
themes.text: Google’s Suncatcher prototype satellite is now online running the Gemma 4 model, Fujifilm is expanding magnetic‑tape capacity fivefold for AI archiving, Core 4 Solutions listed a 300‑rack Nvidia A100 supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million, and CapGrid raised funding to develop drones and data‑centre components.

stories.headline: Google’s Suncatcher prototype satellite is online and runs Gemma 4 model
Fujifilm to boost magnetic tape production fivefold as AI drives data archiving
Core 4 Solutions lists decommissioned Nvidia A100 supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million
CapGrid raises ₹50 cr funding, valued at ₹430 cr to expand into drones and data centres

themes.title: Safety measures target AI misuse
themes.text: OpenAI added stricter limits on weapon‑related advice for teen ChatGPT users, and a malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude VS Code extension was briefly distributed, installing a persistent SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 developers’ machines.

stories.headline: OpenAI tightens weapons‑related information limits for teen ChatGPT users
Anthropic’s Claude VS Code extension backdoored on Cursor, affecting up to 5,000 users
